title: delurio flow graph (flow.yaml)
description: The behaviour of one flow in delurio-graph/0 (SPEC.md §2): states, events, transitions, a finite context, and the guarantees the checker proves. Its meaning is a subset of SCXML.

kind.description: The kind of graph file. A flow.yaml is `flow`.

id.description: The flow's id, by which other flows start it (`starts`) or wait for it (`invoke: { flow }`), and by which its ui.yaml names it.

title.description: The flow in plain words, for people, in the graph's language.

summary.description: What the flow is for, in a few plain sentences.

domain.description: The id of the domain graph (domain.yaml) this flow's `invoke` actions and refusal codes come from; a shared domain sits in its own directory.

ui.description: The id of the UI graph (ui.yaml) of this flow's screens. A flow with no screen (an endpoint, a webhook, an MCP tool, a CI job) has none.

decisions.description: The questions still open in this flow, by id (D1, D2, ...), each with a recommendation and the states it affects.

context.description: The context: a set of variables, each with a finite list of values. Keep it small: a variable stands for the few cases that change behaviour, not for the data itself.

guards.description: Named guards: each an expression (SPEC.md §3) that may name context variables, other guards and `state`.

effects.description: Named effects: each changes the context when a transition that lists it is taken.

failures.description: What each `FAIL.<class>` event stands for, per invoking state: the domain action it comes from, and per class the refusal codes of that action.

initial.description: The state the flow starts in.

states.description: The states of the flow, by id. Nested, parallel and history states are not part of v0.

assertions.description: The guarantees the checker proves: each holds when no reachable configuration (a state and a value for every context variable) satisfies its `never` expression. Under --strict a violated assertion exits 2.

formatVersion.description: The format and its version. Every graph file starts with it.

status.description: `proposed`: written before or apart from the code, nobody has approved it. `captured`: read from existing code (capture mode, every element carries `source`). `approved`: the owner reviewed and accepted it.

identifier.description: An identifier of the graph: English camelCase (SPEC.md §1, Text).

stateRef.description: The id of a state of this flow.

eventName.description: An event: UPPER_SNAKE (SPEC.md §1). A state with `invoke` ends with `DONE` (success) or `FAIL.<class>`, the class being a key under `failures` for that state. `NAVIGATE` is the person leaving the page.

expression.description: An expression of delurio's own language (SPEC.md §3), interpreted, never evaluated as code: or, and, not, ==, !=, in, not in, ( ), [lists], 'strings', numbers, true, false, null, and names (a context variable, a named guard or `state`).
examples: not hasSession or (not fresh and prompt == 'login')

sourceAnchor.description: A source anchor (SPEC.md §9): `<repo-relative path>:<line>`, or a bare `<path>` for a whole file, naming the code that makes the element true. In capture mode every element carries one; in create mode an element carries one when the code already exists.

scalar.description: A value of a context variable: a string, a number or a boolean.

scope.description: What the view shows and how to read what it does not draw.

shows.description: What this view shows, in words.

world.description: `open`: what is not drawn is not ruled out; only `assertions` and `outOfView` are binding. `closed`: the flow is complete.

outOfView.description: What this view leaves out, each in words.

decision.description: A question still open in this flow.

contextVariable.description: A context variable with a finite list of values.

values.description: Every value the variable can take: a finite list, so the checker can visit every reachable configuration.

initial.description: `any` makes the checker start from every value; a fixed value (one of `values`) starts from that one.

say.description: Each value in plain words, for the sentence that describes a starting situation; keyed by the value as text ("true", "false", ...).

effect.description: A change to the context, made when a transition that lists this effect is taken.

set.description: Variables and the values they are given.

havoc.description: Variables that may take any value of their domain (the checker branches into each): a change made elsewhere that the flow cannot know in advance.

failureClasses.description: The failure classes of one invoking state: `from` names the domain action, and each other key is a class (`FAIL.<class>`) listing the refusal codes of that action it stands for.

from.description: The domain action whose refusals the classes stand for.

additionalProperties.description: The refusal codes of the action that this class stands for.

main.description: The main story: the story the page tells first and the path a tutorial and a replay take by default. The events in order from the `given` start; a plain list of events means no `given`. Under --strict it fails when the events cannot be walked.

given.description: The starting situation: a value for context variables whose `initial` is `any`.

events.description: Events, in the order they happen.

state.description: A state of the flow: a step, a screen or an exit.

title.description: The state in words; the id is used when it is missing.

description.description: What happens in the state, in words.

by.description: Who does the step: `human`, `ai`, `agent` or `ci`. A server step with no actor has none.

goal.description: `true` on the state the flow is for, the one it keeps returning to (for flows that never end).

includes.description: What the step covers beyond its title, each in words.

on.description: Event to transition. Not on a final state.

always.description: An ordered list of transitions taken at once, with no event (SCXML's eventless transitions). The first whose guard holds is taken; the list must cover every context, or the flow does not load. Not on a final state.

type.description: `final`: an exit; it has no transitions.

redirect.description: On an exit of a web protocol flow: `success` redirects back with what it carries, `error` redirects with an error code, `never` shows a page and does not redirect.

code.description: On an exit of a web protocol flow: the error code, or several separated by `|`.

carries.description: On a success exit of a web protocol flow: what it carries back.

leavesPage.description: On an exit: `true` when the person left (closed the page, went elsewhere).

allOf.$comment: an exit (type: final) has no transitions and runs nothing
redirect, code, carries and leavesPage are only on an exit (type: final)

invoke.$comment: one of action, flow or external
invoke.description: The step runs something, and ends with `DONE` or `FAIL.<class>`: one of `action`, `flow` or `external`.

action.description: An action of the flow's domain (domain.yaml).

flow.description: Another flow, by id: it runs and this one waits for its outcome.

external.description: Something outside the graphs, by name.

transitionSpec.description: A transition: a target state id, a transition object, or a list of those, tried in document order (the first whose guard holds is taken).

transition.description: A transition (an SCXML transition: a guard is a `cond`, an effect an `<assign>`).

target.description: The state the transition goes to.

guard.description: The transition is taken only when this holds: an expression, or the name of a guard.

effect.description: The effects applied, in order, when the transition is taken.

starts.description: This flow starts another one and does not wait for it (SPEC.md §2, Several flows). The checker finds the started flow by id among the graphs beside this one.

flow.description: The id of the flow started.

given.description: What the started flow begins with: per variable of the started flow, an expression over this flow's context, read where the transition is taken, after its effects. A constant is quoted (`from: "'repo'"`).

additionalProperties.description: An expression over this flow's context, or a constant (a number, a boolean, or a quoted string).

response.description: On a step with no screen: what the outside world sees, as data: `status`, `code`, `redirect`, `headers`, `body`, or the fields of a tool's answer. The page shows it beside the step.

code.description: The error or refusal code answered.

body.description: The body of the answer: its words, or its fields.

id.description: The assertion's id, unique in the flow.

never.description: An expression that no reachable configuration may satisfy.
